subject.title: [Discussion]: Channel-native multi-user model — should messaging platforms be first-class identity sources instead of Control UI?

question: Should OpenClaw extend its shared-gateway identity model so selected channel identities can be linked to durable profiles and participate in authorization, or should channels remain transport-level sender attribution while trusted gateway authentication remains the only shared-user authority?
rationale: This choice sets a long-lived trust, privacy, and authorization boundary across all channels; source evidence shows the existing system intentionally centralizes session enforcement in the gateway, but it does not choose the proposed channel-first product direction.

options.title: Keep gateway authentication primary
options.body: Retain channels as transport and sender-attribution surfaces, while continuing to use trusted gateway authentication for shared-user profiles and session authorization.

options.title: Design opt-in channel identity claims
options.body: Create a scoped design for verified channel claims, explicit profile linking, and per-channel permission semantics without treating platform roles as universal authority.

options.title: Adopt channel-first identity
options.body: Make platform identities the primary multi-user entry point, accepting the larger cross-channel authorization and recovery design program this requires.

recommendation.title: Keep gateway authentication primary
recommendation.body: Retain channels as transport and sender-attribution surfaces, while continuing to use trusted gateway authentication for shared-user profiles and session authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared-gateway identity architecture and related implementation train are directly connected to this decision.
